messages:
alex: Hey — hitting a weird runtime error when using our JS SDK in Cloudflare Workers: `ReferenceError: process is not defined`. Works fine in Node and regular browsers. Minimal repro below. Anyone seen this?

alex: repro:```js
// worker/handler.js
const Redwood = require('@redwood/infer-sdk');
const client = new Redwood.Client({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
await client.generate('hello');
```

megan: Sounds like our auth module reads `process.env` at require-time. CF Workers don't have `process`. We should lazy-read env from the constructor or use `globalThis`.

sam: Also possible the runtime is pulling the CJS build which includes node-only shims. Our `package.json` currently has a single `exports` entry — bundlers can pick the wrong target.

julia: We could use conditional exports like: `{".": {"import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "worker": "./dist/edge/index.mjs"}}`. Some libs add a non-standard `worker` subpath for edge-specific bundles.

alex: Good call. Typing-wise, TypeScript users in ESM-only projects reported that `types` don't resolve when `exports` is present. We should ensure `types": "./dist/index.d.ts"` at the package root and possibly expose subpath types.

megan: We also need to audit for `fs` / `process` / `crypto` usage. Edge runtimes expect Web Crypto and no filesystem. Build an edge bundle that uses `globalThis.crypto.subtle` and avoids node polyfills.

sam: Another real issue: our retry wrapper depends on Node timers + an AbortController polyfill. In some edge runtimes AbortController exists but behaves slightly different and customers saw stuck retries.

alex: Uh — that's bad. We should make retry logic runtime-agnostic and allow injection of a backoff strategy / abort signal from the caller.

julia: For publishing, two main options:
A) Single package publishing multiple artifacts (cjs, esm, edge) and use `exports` conditional mapping.
B) Split into two packages like `@redwood/infer-sdk` and `@redwood/infer-sdk-edge`.
Which feels better?

megan: I lean single package with conditional `exports`. Simpler for users — one install. CI/publishing complexity is manageable.

sam: Split package reduces surface area and keeps the edge bundle tiny. Also clearer semantics for runtime. But adds complexity for docs and versioning.

alex: Onboarding friction story: the starter sample app (starter repo) fails with `wrangler dev` because wrangler resolves the CJS path. Adding `browser` + `import` fields or explicit `exports` should fix it.

deploy-bot: build: @redwood/infer-sdk v2.1.0 published (draft). Exports mapping added to package.json in draft branch. CI results: cjs bundle 120kb, esm bundle 85kb, edge bundle 48kb.

julia: I'm voting single-package + exports + edge subpath. I'll open a PR with build changes: add Rollup target for edge (no node polyfills), ensure `types` emitted to `dist/index.d.ts`, and add tests against Cloudflare/Workers.

megan: I'll add CI matrix: node 14/16/18, deno, cloudflare, vercel edge. Also will add a small sample app for `wrangler dev` in the starter repo so new users can onboard without friction.

sam: +1 :thumbsup: Also we should document known tradeoffs in README (when CJS will be chosen, how to prefer ESM).

alex: Thanks — I'll draft a short RFC describing the three-artifact single-package plan + migration steps for customers. If anyone has specific gotchas (esp. types resolution with `tsconfig` and `exports`), drop them here before I lock the RFC.

megan: One gotcha: TS <4.7 and old bundlers often ignore `exports`, so keep a top-level `main`/`module`/`types` fallback.

sam: And watch subpath exports for `./package.json` resolution — some tools choke on deep imports.

alex: Perfect. I'll include those in the RFC.
